headline: Medium prompt-injection and data-leakage risk: Chatwoot’s customer data can flow into Pipecat’s shared-bus, multi-API voice stack by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Chatwoot can ingest messages and reports, and Pipecat runs a shared-bus, multi-instance conversation pipeline that can consume text from upstream components. That creates a plausible instruction-in-content bridge if Chatwoot output is forwarded into Pipecat without sanitization. The pairwise interaction is not directly documented, so uncertainty pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF Chatwoot content is forwarded into Pipecat as plain text or transcript input
IF Pipecat downstream components parse that text as instructions or tool directives
mitigations: Add a strict content-sanitization step before forwarding Chatwoot text
Prefix forwarded content as untrusted data in the transport layer
Disable any tool-calling on the Pipecat side for Chatwoot-originated turns
requires-engineering: add provenance tags end-to-end
requires-engineering: add allowlisted prompt templates only

B_data_leakage.rationale: Chatwoot touches customer data, contact profiles, interaction history, orders, and messages, while Pipecat touches text, conversation state, audio/video, and can call many third-party STT/LLM/TTS APIs. If the pair shares a workspace or bus, sensitive customer content can be relayed into external inference services. The profiles do not prove a shared filesystem, so this remains medium, not high.
conditions: IF Chatwoot customer records or messages are passed into Pipecat sessions
IF Pipecat is configured to use any external STT/LLM/TTS provider for those sessions
mitigations: Restrict Pipecat to local-only models for Chatwoot-originated traffic
Redact customer identifiers before handoff
Turn off transcript logging for the shared flow
requires-engineering: segregate Chatwoot and Pipecat workspaces
requires-engineering: add DLP checks before any API call

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Chatwoot has broad network egress and API integrations, while Pipecat supports shared-bus multi-instance concurrency and many outbound service adapters. That overlap creates a realistic conflict on shared mutable resources or buses if both are wired to the same backend. The profiles do not show a shared lock or isolated namespace, so the safer choice is medium.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same shared queue, bus, or workspace
IF either agent mutates shared conversation state without external locking
mitigations: Assign separate queues or topics per agent
Use per-agent credentials for all shared services
Add a mutex or lease around shared state writes
requires-engineering: isolate mutable resources by tenant
requires-engineering: add optimistic-concurrency conflict handling

D_cascading_error.rationale: Chatwoot produces customer-facing messages and reports, and Pipecat can consume text/conversation state and route it through speech and LLM services. If Pipecat treats Chatwoot output as authoritative, an upstream hallucination or malformed support reply can cascade into spoken or automated downstream actions. No verification step is documented in either profile, so medium is warranted.
conditions: IF Pipecat consumes Chatwoot-generated text without a verification stage
IF downstream Pipecat components act on that text by speaking, summarizing, or routing it onward
mitigations: Insert a human review step for high-impact Chatwoot outputs
Add schema validation before Pipecat consumes the text
Mark Chatwoot output as untrusted in metadata
requires-engineering: add confidence thresholds before action-taking
requires-engineering: log and diff upstream vs downstream transformations

E_compliance.rationale: Chatwoot clearly touches customer data and interaction history, while Pipecat touches audio, video, text, and analytics and can send data to multiple third-party providers. That creates a plausible retention/residency mismatch for regulated customer communications, even though the profiles do not specify a concrete jurisdiction or certification gap. Uncertainty keeps this at medium.
conditions: IF customer conversations include regulated personal data
IF Pipecat forwards those conversations to external providers with different retention or residency terms
mitigations: Review provider DPAs before enabling the flow
Disable analytics retention for regulated sessions
Minimize stored transcripts and recordings
requires-engineering: route regulated traffic to compliant providers only
requires-engineering: implement deletion/export propagation across both systems
